headline: PARAGUAY IMPEACHMENT CRISIS THREATENS URANIUM ENERGY'S C$17M SOVEREIGN MINERAL INVESTMENT
snippet: President Santiago Peña is facing impeachment proceedings and reportedly submitted his resignation amid a deepening banking crisis in Paraguay — weeks after Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE American: UEC) announced plans to invest C$17 million ($12 million USD) in the country's emerging uranium sector. Paraguay had been pitching itself as a new South American uranium jurisdiction after UEC signed the investment agreement, but the political collapse has thrown the entire programme into doubt. The crisis illustrates the binary jurisdiction risk that often traps junior-focused capital in frontier-market uranium plays: strong geology meets unstable governance at the worst moment. For TSX-V and NYSE American uranium investors who took on exposure through UEC's Paraguay news, the situation is a live reminder that sovereign mineral investment in pre-mining political environments carries a different risk profile than Athabasca Basin or Wyoming ISR assets — regardless of how attractive the resource numbers appear on paper.

headline: FREEPORT APPROVES $4.5B BAGDAD COPPER EXPANSION — DOUBLES ARIZONA MINE OUTPUT, TARGETS MID-2030 PRODUCTION
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan's board approved a $4.5 billion expansion and modernization of the wholly-owned Bagdad copper-molybdenum operation in northwest Arizona, announced November 4-5. The brownfield project will more than double Bagdad's mining and milling rates, adding over 225 million pounds of annual copper production and positioning Bagdad as the second-largest copper mine in the United States behind Morenci. Initial production is targeted for mid-2030 following approximately 3.5 years of construction. The investment follows separate copper announcements for Resolution and signals that majors are now committing capital to new U.S. domestic copper supply in response to critical mineral policy incentives. For TSX-V and ASX copper juniors, the $4.5B Bagdad commitment is the strongest signal yet that large-scale domestic copper development economics are viable at current prices — and that the M&A premium for quality development-stage copper assets continues to build.

headline: RIO TINTO INJECTS $144M INTO RESOLUTION COPPER — FEASIBILITY PHASE BEGINS AFTER ARIZONA LAND WIN
snippet: Rio Tinto approved $144 million for its 55% stake in the Resolution Copper joint venture in Arizona — its share of a larger $261 million JV investment that includes BHP's 45% contribution — following the federal land exchange completed in March 2026 that ended years of legal challenges over Oak Flat. The funds are earmarked for feasibility studies and final design engineering for material handling systems in both exploration shafts, long-lead electrical equipment, water treatment infrastructure, and ongoing exploration drilling. The approval marks the transition from land-access fighting to genuine mine engineering, the first time Resolution has been in this position after two decades of permitting battles. Resolution is projected to be one of the largest copper mines in U.S. history, with an estimated 40 billion pounds of copper resource. Coming one day after Freeport's $4.5B Bagdad announcement, the two decisions together represent a historic week for U.S. domestic copper development.

headline: KAZATOMPROM BUILDS 150,000-TONNE URANIUM STATE RESERVE — STRUCTURAL OVERHANG RISK FOR GLOBAL SPOT PRICE
snippet: Kazakhstan's national uranium company Kazatomprom is laying the groundwork for a 150,000-tonne uranium state reserve, per Energy Intelligence reporting from November 6. If built to that scale, the reserve represents a potential structural overhang for the global spot uranium market — Kazakhstan already supplies approximately 45% of world mine production, and a government reserve of this magnitude would give Astana a Saudi Arabia-style lever over uranium pricing. For junior uranium investors, the news is a double-edged development: bullish for geopolitical supply chain arguments (a Kazakhstan reserve validates the case for Western supply diversification), but bearish for near-term spot price expectations if reserve-building depresses the spot bid-side. At current uranium spot prices near $92/lb, the structural demand thesis from the nuclear renaissance remains intact — but a Kazakh state reserve introduces a new price ceiling variable that investors should model into their TSX-V and ASX uranium project valuations.

headline: UR-ENERGY EYES TOLL MILLING AND WYOMING EXPANSION AFTER SHIRLEY BASIN RESTART — INTERVIEW
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE American: URG / TSX: URE) has restarted its Shirley Basin ISR uranium mine in Wyoming and is now evaluating three paths for further growth: continued exploration drilling to expand Shirley Basin's resource base, strategic acquisitions of additional Wyoming ISR assets, and offering spare processing capacity at the Lost Creek facility to third-party miners as a toll milling service. The Lost Creek facility — which restarted ISR uranium production in 2022 — has processing capacity that now exceeds Shirley Basin's current output, creating a potential revenue stream from toll treating that would reduce unit costs and strengthen Ur-Energy's cost position. The strategy reflects the broader dynamic in Wyoming ISR uranium: a cluster of low-cost ISR deposits and existing infrastructure creates natural synergies that companies like Ur-Energy and Energy Fuels are positioning to monetize. With U.S. utility recontracting underway and long-term uranium prices at $98/lb, toll milling economics at Lost Creek could be attractive for smaller operators without their own processing facilities.

headline: CAMECO NARROWS 2026 GUIDANCE TO 19.5-20.5M LB, SEES WESTINGHOUSE REACTOR BUILDS AS DECADE-LONG GROWTH DRIVER
snippet: Cameco Corporation (TSX: CCO / NYSE: CCJ) narrowed its 2026 attributable uranium production guidance to 19.5–20.5 million pounds of U₃O₈, confirming the company remains on track despite cost pressures in the broader sector. More significantly, Cameco's management highlighted the company's 49% stake in Westinghouse Electric as a structural long-term growth driver: the global pipeline of new reactor builds under Westinghouse technology — the dominant design for Western utility customers — is expected to drive sustained uranium demand growth for the next decade. The Westinghouse stake, acquired in partnership with Brookfield in 2023, positions Cameco as the only publicly traded company with meaningful exposure to both uranium production and reactor services — a vertical integration that most majors lack. For TSX-V uranium juniors, Cameco's confident production guidance and long-term messaging reinforces the demand thesis underpinning project valuation: the nuclear renaissance is structurally different from prior cycles because reactor builds, not just existing fleet refueling, are driving new contracting.

headline: LITHIUM MINERS BOUNCE 1.2% OFF 1-YEAR LOW — ALBEMARLE, SQM WEIGHED BY 2027 GLUT FORECASTS
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) closed at $60.91 on Friday November 6, up 1.21% on the day — a small bounce off a one-year low reached the prior session — but the ETF remains 33.5% below its May 2026 peak, as forecasters project a 2027 oversupply that is weighing on Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) and SQM (NYSE: SQM) valuations. The core bearish argument: lithium spodumene and carbonate production capacity additions committed in 2024–2025 are coming online faster than electric vehicle demand growth in key markets, particularly China where plug-in market share growth has plateaued at around 50%. For junior lithium developers on the TSX-V and ASX, the current environment requires prioritizing projects with sub-$10,000/tonne operating cost structures — anything above that level risks being stranded below future spot prices in a structurally oversupplied market. The key bull rebuttal remains the 2028–2030 demand inflection thesis: lithium demand continues to grow even as short-term oversupply conditions prevail.

headline: MP MATERIALS DROPS 11.9% IN OCTOBER — GOLDMAN SACHS CUTS TARGET AS RARE EARTH BINARY EVENT LOOMS
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) fell 11.9% in October as Goldman Sachs reduced its price target from $65 to $57 and rare earth equities faced sector-wide selling pressure ahead of the November 10 deadline on China's export control suspension. USA Rare Earth shares hit a 52-week low of $9.70 on October 22. The October decline reflects investor positioning ahead of the binary catalyst: if China allows the October 2025 export control suspension to expire without extension, the extraterritorial licensing obligation on foreign-made products using Chinese-origin rare earth materials will resume — a development that would materially improve Western producers' pricing power for heavy rare earths including dysprosium and terbium. MP Materials, which mines and processes light rare earths at Mountain Pass, California, would benefit more indirectly than pure-play heavy rare earth producers. The Goldman price target cut suggests analysts are pricing in the base case of an extension rather than a resumption — meaning any surprise resumption of controls would trigger a sharp re-rating across the sector.

headline: RUSSIA'S URANIUM POSITION FAR DEEPER THAN MINE OUTPUT — ENRICHMENT AND CONVERSION DOMINANCE PERSISTS: C4SA
snippet: A Center for Strategic Advantage report released November 5 warns that Russia's position in the global uranium market is substantially greater than raw mine production data alone suggests — encompassing enrichment, conversion, and reactor export services that Western utilities remain structurally dependent on. Russia mines approximately 6% of global uranium but processes a far larger share of Western utility enrichment needs through Rosatom's TENEX enrichment subsidiary, and continues to export reactor technology that locks in long-term fuel purchase agreements. For junior mining investors building the case for Western uranium development, the C4SA analysis reinforces the structural supply chain argument: mine production independence is only one layer of the geopolitical problem, and the enrichment and conversion capacity gap means even a fully Western-sourced uranium supply chain requires 10–15 years of parallel infrastructure investment. This context supports the valuation case for TSX-V and ASX uranium juniors in stable Western jurisdictions, whose assets represent genuine strategic alternatives to Russian supply chain dependencies.

headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES: SUREBET BC GOLD DISCOVERY EXPANDS 12% WITH 42.31 G/T GOLD DRILL INTERCEPT
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSX-V: GOT) reported new drill results at its Surebet gold discovery in the Golden Triangle of British Columbia, with a headline intercept of 42.31 g/t gold equivalent over 2.00 metres within a broader envelope of 14.61 g/t gold equivalent over 6.00 metres. The company stated the discovery footprint has expanded by 12% based on the new results, with 43 additional drill hole assays still pending — meaning the expansion story has further near-term catalysts ahead. The Golden Triangle in northwestern BC is one of the most prolific gold discovery regions in North America, hosting discoveries including Pretium's Brucejack (now Newmont), Seabridge's KSM, and multiple large-scale development projects. Surebet is at an early but compelling stage: bonanza-grade intercepts are present, the system is growing, and the upcoming resource estimate work will determine whether the geology translates into an economic deposit. At $4,070/oz gold, the economics of a high-grade BC discovery like Surebet are more compelling than at any prior point in the exploration cycle.
